CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 32% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 68% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Calgary’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Calgary has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 2.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 6.3 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: Wallstedt makes it eight straight wins
paras: Joel Eriksson Ek got the scoring started for the Wild just 25 seconds into the game, and Quinn Hughes stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the first. Šimon Nemec got the Flames on the board late in the period, but they got no closer. Ryan Hartman and Martin Pospíšil fought at the end of the first. Kirill Kaprizov made it 3-1 for the Wild on the power play early in the second, and Matt Boldy added an empty-net goal with 49 seconds left to make it 4-1. Kaprizov and Boldy each had a goal and two assists.

The Flames had a little more of the play, but the Wild had the finish. Jesper Wallstedt made 22 saves for the Wild, and Dustin Wolf stopped 18 of 21 at the other end. Wallstedt has won eight straight starts. The Wild improved to 17-3-4 and climbed into first in the NHL in points, while the Flames dropped to 10-12-1, slipping to sixth in the Pacific.
